text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after climbing 15.6% over two weeks, giving back some gains as geopolitical diesel supply news shifted. Yesterday the stock hit $463, its peak in this run, as Trump announced a deal with Putin to import Russian diesel into U.S. markets — a move aimed at easing tight fuel supplies and high prices. Today's pullback likely reflects investors digesting the complications: reports that the deal may contradict existing Russia sanctions law, and Ukraine's public criticism of the arrangement, which introduces uncertainty about whether the agreement will actually hold or face political pushback.

The underlying picture for refiners remains tight but complicated. U.S. refineries are running near capacity at 92.7%, and diesel stocks are historically low at 105 million barrels, while wars in Eastern Europe and the Middle East have taken offline refining capacity globally. The Trump-Putin diesel deal was framed as a lifeline to ease those constraints — but legal and geopolitical clouds over it now make that relief less certain, which may explain why the market is taking profits on yesterday's enthusiasm.
